anomaly_def.Name: Database Memory Allocation Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description: Definition: Root cause located at the engine memory-allocation layer, where the total amount of physical memory or swap consumed by buffer caches, plan caches, per-session work areas, sort and hash buffers, temporary structures, parallel workers, and background heaps exceeds the safe envelope of the host. It addresses the size and growth of memory regions and is distinct from how efficiently buffer pages are accessed or serialized. Observable phenomena: sustained operating-system memory pressure, paging or swapping activity, out-of-memory termination events, continuous growth of database-process resident-set size, declining cache hit ratios driven by allocation churn, memory-pressure-induced CPU stalls, and node eviction or abnormal restarts in clustered or virtualized deployments. Possible contributing factors: per-query work memory left uncapped and amplified by high concurrency, runaway hash or sort operations materializing in memory, excessive parallel workers each reserving private buffers, plan-cache bloat caused by un-parameterized ad-hoc statements, session leaks or long-lived sessions holding cursor and array state, in-memory column store or result cache mis-sized for the workload, and memory leaks within user-defined functions, extensions, or stored procedures.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with insufficient memory headroom, buffer pressure, oversized intermediate state, or memory-allocation constraints inside the engine or client library.
entry.solution_guidance: Check memory availability, per-session memory settings, large sorts or hashes, and whether workload concurrency is amplifying memory consumption.
